note: WP-26: each platform's AI-disclosure setting, when it is required, and what we do. required_when: realistic (content that could pass as real people, places or events: our drawn characters do not), realistic_audio (also realistic-sounding generated audio, such as a synthetic narrating voice), or never. we_disclose_anyway: turn the setting on whenever a synthetic voice or model-made picture is in the film, even where not required (the studio's choice). checked: the date the source page was read and what it said; 'unverified' where the page could not be read. Policies change: re-read the sources when a platform changes its rules.

youtube.note: 'We require creators to disclose AI-generated or altered content that seems realistic'; non-realistic content such as a fully animated video is exempt; content with C2PA metadata may be labelled automatically (a label that cannot be adjusted); the page does not address synthetic narrating voices

tiktok.note: unverified: the help page could not be read from here (it redirects to a page that renders no text); treated cautiously: the label is turned on whenever a synthetic voice is used

instagram.note: 'Meta requires you to label content you share that has photorealistic video or realistic-sounding audio that has been digitally generated or altered'; its examples include 'a reel narrated with a realistic AI-generated voiceover'; cartoon-style video is not required; 'industry-standard signals' in a file are read to label it

facebook.note: Meta's policy, as Instagram's (the business help page that described it for Facebook no longer exists)

x.note: unverified: the synthetic and manipulated media policy page refused the request; the caption line says what is synthetic

linkedin.setting: none (shows a C2PA icon on content with Content Credentials)
linkedin.note: 'Image and video content that is cryptographically signed using C2PA Content Credentials will be noted with the C2PA icon', visible to every viewer; rolling out gradually
